title: Counting the Cost of the Tower
text:
Large crowds were following Jesus, and he turned and spoke to them about what it would really cost to be his disciple. He did not want followers who started out with enthusiasm and gave up halfway. To make the point, he told two short stories.

Suppose one of you wants to build a tower, he said. Would you not first sit down and estimate the cost, to see whether you have enough money to finish it? Otherwise, you might lay the foundation and then be unable to complete the work. Then everyone who saw the bare foundation would mock you, saying: this man began to build and was not able to finish.

Or suppose a king is about to go to war against another king. Will he not first sit down and consider whether, with ten thousand men, he can stand against an enemy coming at him with twenty thousand? If he cannot, then while the other king is still a long way off, he will send envoys and ask for terms of peace.

In both cases, the sensible person sits down before acting, counts honestly, and decides on that basis whether to begin at all.
lesson: Before starting a project or a fight, sit down and add up what it will truly take. If you cannot finish, it is wiser to negotiate early than to leave a monument to your misjudgment.
people: Jesus, a builder, a king going to war
location: Galilee and Judea (modern Israel and Palestinian territories)
